title: The Baptism of the Lord
hook: the Christmas season ends at the Jordan
tomorrow: Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Epiphany: magi, not kings, and three gifts that told a whole life. Your line was gold, frankincense, myrrh.

In some homes, Christmas ends when the tree goes out to the curb, right after New Year's. In the Church it lasts longer, and it doesn't end with a party. It ends at a river. One week the baby is in the manger with magi kneeling. A few days later on the calendar, he's a grown man of about thirty, wading into the river in a line of people who've come to confess their sins. The next morning the green vestments come out and Ordinary Time begins. Today is the hinge.
screen: `THE TREE AT THE CURB.` → `FROM MANGER TO RIVER.` → `THE HINGE OF THE SEASON.`

segments.voice: John the Baptist was out by the Jordan, calling people to turn their lives around and plunging them in the river as a sign. The Greek word baptizō means to dip or immerse. Then Jesus walks up and gets in line. Matthew says John tried to stop him. In the Douay-Rheims: "I ought to be baptized by thee, and comest thou to me?" Readers still ask it: if Jesus had no sin, why go through a baptism of repentance? Jesus answers that it's fitting, to fulfill all justice, and John lets him. Catholic tradition gives several answers to the why. He stood in line with sinners, in solidarity, taking his place among them. He went into the water not to be made clean but to make the waters holy, so that later baptisms would carry his life. Then he comes up out of the water, the heavens open, the Spirit comes down like a dove, and a voice says: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." Christian tradition sees all three here: the Son in the river, the Spirit as a dove, the Father's voice. Notice when the voice comes: before any miracle, before any sermon, before a single public act. In Matthew's order, the voice first, then the work. For Catholics, that's the shape of every baptism too: a person claimed and loved before they've accomplished anything. Christmas was about God showing up; the baptism is where the grown man steps forward.
screen: `BAPTIZŌ: TO DIP, TO PLUNGE.` · `JOHN TRIES TO STOP HIM.` · `NOT TO BE CLEANSED, BUT TO BLESS.` · `THE VOICE BEFORE THE WORK.` · then, large: `THIS IS MY BELOVED SON.`

segments.voice: If you're baptized, recall what you know of the day, the church, who held you, your godparents' names; Catholics renew their baptismal promises each Easter, saying no to sin and yes to the faith, and if you pray, you can quietly say yes again. If you're not baptized, or would rather not say, wash your hands slowly or touch a little water, and remember the order in the story: the voice before the work.
Baptizo, to dip. The Greek root of baptism: Jesus wading into the Jordan with sinners, the feast that closes the Christmas season. Today's word.
Your line: the season ends in water. Next comes green, and Ordinary Time. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the Baptism of the Lord on the Sunday after the Epiphany (or the Monday, when the Epiphany falls on January 7 or 8); it ends the Christmas season, and Ordinary Time begins the next day.

notes: Date rule: the Sunday after January 6; in countries where the Epiphany is moved to a Sunday falling on January 7 or 8, the Baptism is kept on the following Monday. Confirm.
'To make the waters holy' reflects patristic teaching (e.g. Ignatius of Antioch, Ephesians 18) and CCC 1224; confirm.
Baptismal promises renewed at Easter (Easter Vigil and Easter Sunday Masses). Confirm.
